name: Gevrey-Chambertin

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Pinot Noir sits in its sweet spot, so the wines can show the style it is known for.

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
Bourgogne, village, Premier Cru, Grand Cru
Burgundy's four levels, from regional Bourgogne up through village wines to Premier Cru and Grand Cru vineyards.
keyfacts: The Route des Grands Crus runs through the Grands Crus, separating Chambertin from Charmes-Chambertin.
Chambertin-Clos de Bèze may also be sold as Chambertin, and Mazoyères-Chambertin as Charmes-Chambertin, but not the other way round.
Twenty-six climats are classified as Premier Cru.

notes: Gevrey-Chambertin reds are deeply colored and potent for Burgundy.
They have intense aromas and flavors of blackcurrant, cherry, musk and licorice.

blurb.text: A Côte de Nuits appellation for red wine made from Pinot Noir. It holds nine Grand Cru vineyards, Chambertin and eight others, and has many village-level vineyards, since it stretches far east.
